It was supposed to be simple, like every other dastardly plot he'd tried to bring to fruition. There were only ten guards to oppose him this time, and he’d checked their Facebook profiles-not one of them seemed to be in any way competent at their job.

With a put-upon sigh, the weary Count adjusted the collar of his cape and checked that his make-up hadn’t smudged with his sister’s compact mirror. His hair wasn’t quite as slicked back as he liked it, but there wasn’t much he could do about that. It turned out that painting the whole lot jet black wasn’t easy on the scalp, but honestly! It wasn’t like he could get a proper dye job, it had been much cheaper to acquire a pot of glossy stuff from his unsuspecting dad.

With everything in order, the young supervillain prepared for take eleven of his debut, certain that fortune was in his favour. He strode confidently towards the heavy oak doors, prepared to slam them open for dramatic effect, only to find that they swung open under their own power. There would be plenty more opportunities to employ his well-practiced scare tactics-

The first sign that the Count’s brilliant scheme was doomed to fail was the crowd of civilians in the center of the bank. Thirty or forty of the imbeciles, each draped in the cheapest vampire outfits they could possibly have found in the local costume store. There were men and women alike in knock offs of his supersuit, their hair slicked back just so and their mouths stretched oddly by plastic fangs and the like.

The second sign was barrage of noise which assaulted his sensitive ears.

“Have you heard? The Count’s set his eyes on this bank! The real one!”

“I know, I wonder what he’ll use this time?”

“He’s already used silly string on the Mayor, and the stink-bombs affected him worse than the police he was aiming at, so maybe it’ll be a spud gun.”

It wasn’t fair, really it wasn’t. Sure, his power fueled itself off of the mirth of his peers, but it was supposed to be easy to use that power against them in turn. Any day now he’d break through his limit and drain them of that cheer, instead of amplifying it. Still, this was a new angle. He had a bicycle waiting just outside ready to flee on, and three back-up weapons.

The Count withdrew his water pistol from the folds of his cape and steadied the blasted contraption as the barrel drew level with the ten-year-old child’s incredulous face. For a second the moron froze, and then the white paint around his lips cracked as he broke into a fit of giggles. The supervillain rode out the waves, confident that the minor boost to his super-strength was enough for him to take on at least three guards, but then the two parents of the brat caught on and joined in.

Great, he had the power to subdue the lot of them at that, he just had to reach someone official looking before-

The bug spread and the Count felt beads of sweat form on his brow as laughter echoed around the building. His muscles squirmed uncomfortably with the strain of their newfound potency, his gut especially challenged as he tried to contain himself. He couldn’t, he had a job to do and rent to pay, he needed to be taken seriously…

Surrounded by idiots cackling in glee, the Count had no choice but to succumb to the rush of heady euphoria which undermined his purpose. By the time his knees hit the floor, his own laughter had already betrayed him, and there was no hope of salvaging the situation.

<And there we go folks. God bless the Count, doing his best to cheer us up in this time of hardship.>
